name: Microsoft 365
sub: Entra ID · Microsoft Graph · Outlook · OneDrive · Teams
headline: Registering the app takes an hour. The slow parts are the Partner Center identity check and each customer's admin consent.
needGuide: Yes. Since 2025, Microsoft's default consent policy stops users approving mail, calendar, file and chat scopes themselves, so you need an admin-consent flow.
authDetail: Authorization code with PKCE, through MSAL. Refresh tokens rotate on each use and expire after 90 days of inactivity. Access tokens last 60–90 minutes. Use the /organizations or /common authority.
timeToProduction: 1–4 weeks, plus admin approval at each customer
cost: Registration and publisher verification are free. You need a work tenant. Optional Microsoft 365 Certification costs an auditor fee plus a penetration test (one quote was about US$6,800).

tiers.label: User-consentable scopes
tiers.note: Needs a verified publisher. Works for personal accounts and for tenants with relaxed consent settings.

tiers.label: Admin-consent path (typical)
tiers.time: Days to weeks for each customer
tiers.note: Blocked by the Microsoft-managed default consent policy, so each customer's admin has to approve.

tiers.label: Application (app-only) permissions
tiers.note: Always needs admin consent and gives tenant-wide access. Customers rarely accept it for agents.

prereqs: A company work tenant with a verified custom domain. That same domain becomes your publisher domain.
MFA for everyone who uses admin portals, CLI or infrastructure-as-code. It is mandatory.
A Partner Center account in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program. The primary contact's email must be on your domain, and the legal name and address must match your registration exactly.
An HTTPS callback host, plus privacy statement and terms of service URLs.
A second tenant to act as a customer during testing.

steps.do: In Partner Center, enroll in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program with a work account from your tenant. Upload incorporation and domain documents and complete ID verification; your name must match your government ID exactly. Then associate your tenant.
Assign directory roles: Application Developer for developers, and Cloud Application Administrator for whoever will verify the publisher. Check that MFA works for all of them.

Go to entra.microsoft.com → Entra ID → App registrations → New registration. For supported account types, choose “Multiple Entra ID tenants” (add personal accounts only if you need consumers). Set the redirect URI to Web: https://app.yourco.com/auth/microsoft/callback, then click Register.
Under Owners → Add owners, add at least 2 work accounts. Don't use personal accounts: an app registered with one can never be publisher-verified.
Under Authentication, add the prod, staging and http://localhost redirect URIs. HTTPS is required except for localhost. Multitenant apps can't use wildcards, and the localhost port is ignored.
Under Certificates & secrets, use a certificate or federated credential for production. Client secrets last at most 24 months (12 is recommended), and the value is shown once. Store it in Key Vault.

Under API permissions → Microsoft Graph → Delegated, add openid, profile, email, offline_access, User.Read and your feature scopes. Don't click “Grant admin consent” in your home tenant unless you're testing there.
Fill in Branding & properties: name, logo, home page, terms and privacy URLs. Set the publisher domain to your verified domain, or host /.well-known/microsoft-identity-association.json.

Implement an MSAL confidential client with authorization code and PKCE. Validate the issuer for each tenant, persist rotated refresh tokens encrypted, and handle invalid_grant and claims challenges (declare cp1).

Build a “Connect your organization” button that opens https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/v2.0/adminconsent?client_id=…&scope=https://graph.microsoft.com/.default&redirect_uri=…&state=… and a page that tells non-admins how to request approval.
In a second tenant, sign in as a non-admin (expect “Approval required”), as an admin using /adminconsent, and with a personal Microsoft account. Then check Enterprise apps → your app → Permissions.

phases.name: Verify the publisher
phases.duration: Minutes, after Partner Center shows Authorized

steps.do: In your app, open Branding & properties → Add Partner ID to verify publisher. Enter the PartnerGlobal ID (Partner Center → Account settings → Identifiers), then click Verify and save. Do this in the same session as your MFA sign-in.
Optional: complete Publisher Attestation and Microsoft 365 Certification if enterprise buyers or the Teams store ask for them.

Keep a calendar for rotating secrets and certificates. Leave app instance property lock on (the default for new apps since June 2026). Watch for sign-in failures caused by customers' Conditional Access policies.

consoleRoles.can: Fully manage one app (up to 100 owners)
consoleRoles.who: 2 or more engineers, on work accounts

consoleRoles.can: Create app registrations even when users are blocked from doing so, and manage apps they own
Manage all app registrations and verify the publisher
Same as Cloud Application Administrator, plus application proxy
Grant consent for any permission, including Graph app roles, and change consent settings

consoleRoles.role: Partner Center: AI Cloud Partner Program Admin / Accounts Admin
consoleRoles.can: Manage the partner account used for verification

roles.team: The Owner and Legal handle Partner Center identity. A Cloud Application Administrator verifies the publisher. Developers hold Application Developer and own the app. Security handles certificates and Key Vault. Design provides branding. Support writes the admin-consent guide that customers' IT teams will read.
roles.console: Entra roles: App registration Owners, Application Developer, Cloud Application Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator, plus Partner Center admin roles. Add owners under App registrations → your app → Owners, or with the Graph call POST /applications/{id}/owners/$ref.
roles.customer: Customers' tenant admins control user consent (Enterprise apps → Consent and permissions). They approve requests through the admin consent workflow, or grant tenant-wide consent through /adminconsent. Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator is needed for application permissions.

testing: Microsoft 365 E5 developer sandbox: available to Visual Studio Professional and Enterprise subscribers and eligible partners. It includes 25 licenses and lasts 90 days, renewable.
A second trial tenant can stand in for a customer. Test as a non-admin and as an admin.
A personal Microsoft (outlook.com) account works for mail, calendar and OneDrive. Teams chats are not supported for personal accounts.
Use Graph Explorer to prototype calls. Use prompt=consent to force the consent screen, but only while testing.
To pilot with specific customers, restrict access using “Allow only certain tenants (Preview)”.
customer: The default for new tenants is “Let Microsoft manage your consent settings”. It blocks user consent for Mail.*, Calendars.*, Files.Read.All, Sites.*.All, Chat.*, OnlineMeetings.*, Contacts, People and Tasks. Microsoft rolled this out between July 2025 and July 2026.
Multitenant apps whose publisher isn't verified are pushed to admin consent. Users see AADSTS90094 or “Need admin approval”.
If the tenant has the admin consent workflow turned on, users see “Approval required” and can send a request with a justification.
The tenant-wide admin consent URL returns admin_consent=True&tenant=… Never use /common for this URL.
Conditional Access policies (compliant device, location, sign-in frequency) can block or re-prompt your users. You can't control these.

scopesTable.note: Blocked by the Microsoft-managed default policy
Or use Sites.Selected plus a grant per site

review.when: Microsoft doesn't review Graph apps. Publisher verification is an identity check that requires a fully verified Partner Center account, an associated tenant, a matching publisher domain, the right role and MFA. Microsoft 365 Certification is optional.

timeline.label: Partner Center verification
timeline.reported: 1 day to several weeks; some accounts stall

timeline.label: Publisher verification
timeline.reported: Minutes, once Partner Center shows Authorized

timeline.label: Microsoft 365 Certification (optional)
timeline.reported: Needs a penetration test from the last 12 months

review.recurring: Verification itself doesn't need renewing. Publisher Attestation and Microsoft 365 Certification renew every year, with reminders at 90, 60 and 30 days. Rotate secrets and certificates before they expire.

blockers.fix: The Partner Center primary contact's email domain must be a verified domain in your tenant.
Wait until Legal info shows Authorized, and use the PartnerGlobal ID, not a location ID.

blockers.problem: The “Add Partner ID” button is missing
blockers.fix: The app was registered with a personal account. Register it again in your work tenant.
Your own admin has blocked multitenant apps. Ask for an exclusion under Application policies.
Make your name, including any middle name, match your government ID, and use the legal entity name, not the brand name.

blockers.problem: Users hit AADSTS90094 or “Need admin approval”
blockers.fix: This is expected under the default policy. Send them to your admin-consent flow.

gotchas: Refresh tokens expire after 90 days without use, and resetting a user's password revokes them. For single-page apps they last a fixed 24 hours.
Outlook throttling is 10,000 requests per 10 minutes per app per mailbox, with a maximum of 4 concurrent requests.
Apps that allow personal accounts are limited to 2 secrets, 30 permissions per API, and redirect URIs without query strings.
Tenant-wide admin consent can replace permissions that were granted earlier.
An app object can't be moved to another tenant later, so register it in the right tenant first.
agentCan: Register the app with az ad app create or Terraform, add owners, redirect URIs and permissions through Graph, write the MSAL and admin-consent code, draft the admin-consent guide for customers' IT teams, and track secret rotation.
humanMust: Complete Partner Center enrollment and ID verification, set the publisher domain in the portal, verify the publisher with MFA, test with real sign-ins, and sign attestations.
uncertain: Microsoft can change which permissions the default consent policy blocks at any time.
The docs disagree on whether a Global Administrator or a Privileged Role Administrator must approve Graph application permissions through the workflow.
The cheapest way to get a work tenant without paying isn't confirmed.
It's unclear whether Microsoft will push third-party agents toward Entra Agent ID blueprints.
